title: QBR metrics ops playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose
---
This is a working draft playbook for Customer Success leads to use during QBRs and renewal conversations. Focus: standardize definitions for the four core operational KPIs we track across accounts (latency, uptime, cost/token, cache hit rate), provide calculation recipes, recommended measurement windows and targets, and include a simple KPI table template to slot into customer decks.

Scope and audience
---
Audience: CSMs, Solutions Engineers (SEs), Account Execs (AEs) prepping QBRs.
Scope: Hosted + Dedicated + Private deployments. Notes on variations for Private customers (data access gaps).
Status: Draft — please add comments inline or link Jira tickets for follow-ups.

How to use this doc
---
- Pull the numbers from Redwood Console (per-route/model dashboards) and billing dataset.
- When in doubt, prefer production traffic over synthetic tests for QBRs. Synthetic tests are useful for isolating regressions but should be labeled separately in slides.
- Show rolling 30/90-day windows depending on customer preference; include recent 7-day snapshot for trends.

Metric definitions (single-line summaries + formal calc)
---
1) Latency (effective request latency)
   - Summary: Per-request end-to-end generation latency observed by the platform for user-facing requests (includes queuing/batching time + inference time + post-processing).
   - Calculation: Report p50, p95, p99 over chosen window.
   - Formula: For window W, pX = Xth percentile of {end_time - request_time} for all user requests in W. Exclude known maintenance windows and synthetic probe traffic.
   - Notes: For chat flows show turn-level latencies and session-level 95th percentiles. Break out streaming vs non-streaming if both are used.

2) Uptime (availability)
   - Summary: Percent of observed requests that received a successful 2xx response within the SLA budget.
   - Calculation: uptime% = 100 * (successful_requests_within_SLA / total_requests_attempted) for window W.
   - SLA budget: default SLA = 99.9% for Dedicated/Hosted customers with SLA contracts; for PLG/no-SLA show internal goal of 99.5%.
   - Exclusions: planned maintenance (documented) and customer-side networking failures (if verifiable).

3) Cost per token (unit economics)
   - Summary: Platform-side cost per generated token for the account (not list price). Used to explain spend, optimization opportunities and renewal uplift conversations.
   - Calculation (simplified): cost_per_token = (compute_costs + amortized_reserved_costs + storage_costs_for_caches) / total_generated_tokens_in_window.
   - Data sources: billing export + infra cost allocation model (see linked Confluence page CONFLUENCE-5243 for allocation rules).
   - Notes: For Dedicated reserved instances include amortized reservation cost; for hosted use per-request compute estimate. Show both gross and optimized (after cache + batching) numbers when available.

4) Cache hit rate (inference-level cache)
   - Summary: Fraction of requests served (partially or fully) from prefix/KV cache so that incremental token compute was reduced.
   - Calculation: cache_hit_rate = 100 * (requests_with_cache_hit / total_applicable_requests).
   - More granular: token-level cache savings = 1 - (tokens_generated_when_cache_used / tokens_generated_if_no_cache). This requires a simulation model — indicate if metric is estimated.
   - Notes: For customers using session-level caching or application-side prefixing, ensure the dataset filters to applicable routes only.

Measurement windows and percentiles
---
- Standard QBR windows: 30-day (primary), 90-day (trend), last 7-day (recent behavior).
- Latency: present p50/p95/p99. Uptime: present overall% and hourly incident counts. Cost: show total spend and cost_per_token. Cache: show daily hit rate trend and hit-rate distribution across top routes.

Sample KPI table (paste into slides)
---
Columns: Metric | Window | Value | Target | Delta | Notes
Example rows (text table):
Metric | Window | Value | Target | Delta | Notes
Latency (p95) | 30d | 580 ms | <= 500 ms | +80 ms | Peak after v1.3 rollout
Uptime | 90d | 99.92% | 99.9% | +0.02% | SLA met (no credit)
Cost / token | 30d | $0.0038 | $0.0025 (goal) | +52% | High due to low cache on route /chat/generate
Cache hit rate | 30d | 18% | >= 35% | -17 pp | Recommend prefixing + longer session caches

Quick calculation cheatsheet (copyable)
---
- p95 latency: order the latencies, take 95th percentile. (Console -> traces -> latency histogram)
- Uptime%: (success_within_SLA / total_attempts) * 100
- Cost/token (raw): total_inferred_compute_costs / total_generated_tokens
- Cache hit rate: requests_with_cache_flag / total_requests_for_route

Recommended targets by customer tier (guideline)
---
- PLG / SMB: Latency p95 <= 700ms; Uptime >= 99.5%; Cost/token aim <$0.005; Cache hit >= 20%
- Mid-market: Latency p95 <= 500ms; Uptime >= 99.8%; Cost/token aim <$0.0035; Cache hit >= 30%
- Enterprise (SLA-backed): Latency p95 <= 300-400ms (negotiable per workload); Uptime >= 99.9% (or contractual); Cost/token discussed as committed economics; Cache hit >= 35%

Playbook actions (when KPI breaches)
---
1) Latency spike (p95 up > +20% vs baseline):
   - Owner: SE + Eng on-call if infra-related
   - Runbook steps: check recent deploys (PR ids), view slow routes, compare synthetic probe latencies, escalate to serving-runtime team with trace ids.
   - Quick mitigations: route traffic to fallback model variant, increase burst capacity, toggle batching settings.

2) Uptime dip (>=1 hour outage or rolling 0.5% drop):
   - Owner: SRE + CSM (communications)
   - Steps: verify maintenance windows, collect error counts, open incident ticket and notify customer; document for QBR.

3) Cost/token drift (>25% vs quarter):
   - Owner: CSM + Solutions Eng
   - Steps: check cache and batching levels, verify model variant usage, propose quantization or lower-cost variant for non-critical routes, run cost projection for renewal.

4) Low cache hit rate (<target):
   - Owner: SE + CSM
   - Steps: identify top non-hitting routes, recommend prefixing of common prompts, increase TTLs, instrument suggestions for app-side session stitching.

How to present for renewal conversations
---
- Show both unit economics (cost/token) and business impact (e.g., expected monthly spend at current growth).
- Frame optimizations as incremental levers: caching, batching, model variant, reserved capacity. Tie each lever to expected % savings.
- Include an action plan with owner and timeline (30/60/90 days) and measurable targets.

Common data caveats and FAQs
---
- Private deployments: we may not have full infra cost visibility; use agreed-on allocation model and mark estimates clearly.
- Synthetic traffic: always separate in dashboards and clearly label in QBR slides.
- Multi-model routes: when multiple model variants are used behind one path, show weighted average and break out top contributors.

Appendix — example query snippets (high-level)
---
- tokens_generated = SUM(generated_tokens) GROUP BY date
- p95_latency = APPROX_PERCENTILE(latency_ms, 0.95)
(Note: concrete SQL depends on internal billing/observability schema — ask analytics if missing fields.)

Notes and small hacks from field
---
- Customers respond well to a split slide: left side trend charts, right side top 3 actions + expected savings.
- When talking cost/token, also present an "efficiency ratio" (tokens per $100) so non-technical execs can grasp impact.

End of draft — comments welcome.
